reports.lens: batch4-live-check: A1 whole-word ids refusal, A5 per-item test-count ratchet, A2 return-route sentence, A3 Improve child dir at emit, A4 test-strategy host-tool probe Done-when, A6 harness (reap, preflight, SIGTERM)
reports.summary: Scorecard. A1 not exercised (no ids refusal fired; the rule text was never displayed and both models titled tests with standalone ids anyway). A5 working as a silent computation (accepted_ran on 6 of 11 verify records per run, no refusal, no false refusal, no count ever dropped); its refusal route is not exercised. A2 partly working: the sentence is true and in 45/45 and 47/47 packets, no false 'commit before the return' lesson in either knowledge home, Checkers made 0 model commits and ShipLoop committed the leftovers itself; but Battleship hand-committed twice (README.md at integrate, test/system.test.js at system-test-author), the first following the integrate row's own instruction, so the design's acceptance criterion (authors only 'ShipLoop Workspace') is met in 1 of 2 runs. A3 working: the child directory was born at improve-bind (15 s before the model's own mkdir) in both runs, and no 'No such file' on opening.md fired; the models still mkdir defensively in 8 of 8 children, so the 'no mkdir in a wrapper' half of the criterion is unmet and uninformative. A4 split: Checkers probed headless Chrome against a stand-in, cited the output, recorded 'No access gap', then really used Chrome in system tests (ST-2) and ended with unverified []; Battleship saw the same Done-when entry in its head and sidestepped by classifying the UI as 'no host tool needed', never probed a browser (installed on the same host), and ended with an unprobed access gap; the in-run Improve review accepted it. A6: reap working (Battleship leaked two servers via the models' `& ... kill %1`, both reaped and recorded in result.json left_behind and the harness 'left' line; Checkers none), but left_behind is absent from facts.md/metrics.json/review-export, and a live SIGTERM hit an adjacent concurrent Grok harness (caused by the Checkers model's `pkill -f "node server.js"` matching the harness argv, which embeds the checks), which the new handler handled exactly as designed (host group ended, 'terminated by SIGTERM', resumable). The cause, a harness argv that matches generic kill patterns plus cross-track concurrency, is a defect left to a documentation-only sequencing rule. Both runs passed all verdicts (ShipLoop done, committed, checks pass), but that is evidence, not the goal: the faithful-fidelity gaps are A2 (integrate row vs route sentence), A4 (classification sidestep), and the A6 argv/cross-run hazard.

findings.where: skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_stage_spec.py:413 (integrate Develop line); shiploop_navigator._item_commit printing 'Not committed (changed, but not in the step plan's paths)'; BS [383]; BS work commit de38128
findings.evidence: MEASURED. Battleship's first model commit (de38128 'Document Battleship run, API and tests in README', author Jim Wiese, not 'ShipLoop Workspace') was made at integrate with `git -C $W add README.md && git commit` [383]. The integrate packet head says (BSR/packets/nav-0f266240...md line 19) 'ShipLoop commits the item's changed files that the step plan's paths declare ... do not write that commit yourself. It names any other changed file: commit the ones the product needs, delete generated output.' README.md was written by the document stage and was not in the step plan's paths (in Checkers the step plan declared README, so nothing was undeclared). So ShipLoop's own row tells the model to hand-commit undeclared files while the route sentence says to commit nothing for the return and plan-return commits leftovers. A second defect in the same message: after the model had already committed README.md, ShipLoop still printed 'Not committed (changed, but not in the step plan's paths): README.md. Commit the ones the product needs' in the same result [383] (git log in that result shows de38128 below 65cd022): item_scope.commit_item computes undeclared from changed paths, not from what is still uncommitted. The harness counts this as model_glue (metrics.json model_glue[0], 'git commit/add by the model'), so a ShipLoop-instructed commit is scored as glue.
findings.generic_fix: Make the integrate row and the route sentence say one thing: leftover product files are committed by plan-return (or by integrate itself), and the model commits nothing; compute the 'not committed' notice from files that are actually still uncommitted, and name it only for files plan-return will skip (credential-like, excluded).

findings.where: test/shiploop_e2e/run.py (harness argv carries every --check string); CK [548], [569], [598]; r3-battleship-grok-none/result.json
findings.evidence: MEASURED. The harness command line embeds the case's --check commands, which contain 'node server.js' (the pgrep output at CK [548] shows 5841's argv including '--check PORT=39171 node server.js > /dev/null ...'). The Checkers model's own memory note (written at [598]) says the pkill 'terminated three node server.js processes of a concurrent Battleship run (and matched its harness's command line)' and was 'done to clean up a server that had already exited'. So a generic kill pattern a model chooses by habit kills a sibling harness; the design (G8-harness.json for_against) anticipated this and left it to the SPEC/README sequencing rule only, but the sequencing was honored for the Sonnet pair (Battleship 23:19:57-23:32:35, Checkers 23:32:48-23:47) and not across tracks: r3-battleship-grok-none started 4 s before the Sonnet Battleship and ran through the whole Checkers run. The A6-sentence (a ShipLoop line telling models to kill only pids they started) was dropped by design. The kill cost the Grok run a restart (stopped at test-author) and invalidates its wall-time.
findings.generic_fix: Keep model-patternable text out of the harness process: pass checks by file or environment, or set a neutral process title, so no generic pkill -f/pgrep -f pattern a model writes can match a harness; run tracks that share a machine in separate process-visible namespaces or serially. Reopen the 'kill only pids you started' packet line only if this recurs with the argv fixed.

VERDICT. The run passed (38 accepted actions, 36 accepted at first submit, 2 refusals, both cured by the first remedy), and it passed faithfully: no hand git commit or add, no state edit, no forced pass, no app-specific rule needed. Unattended (asked_user []), inline (no agents), planning window 340 s (5.7 min against the 30 min rule), 36% of it in Improve.

TENET. Structurally the five elements are present in every packet: all 38 producer packets carry Goal, Done-when, Checked-by, Considerations (not skill-assess, skill-validate, handoff), result path + template + Allowed outcomes, Recovery command, Pause, Halt (facts.md: where/purpose/operates/checked/produces/recovery 38 of 38, inputs 37). The 8 Improve parents add the Done-when (I2: 'correct the result, never the condition'), a Checked-by, the opening/evidence/commit/callback/restart-stopped route, and the child's runtime JSON restates work, exit/repeat conditions, scope, authority, done_argv, next_argv. The defects are at content level, and they share one cause: the model opened the packet file for only 15 of 38 producer packets (23 were run from the printed head, usually cut by its own wrapper to 12-14 lines), so anything not in the first ~14 lines (Goal, Done-when, Checked-by, Considerations) is effectively absent. Findings: Checked-by understates real gates (T2, recurrence of r2 B10); body-only duties skipped (release-check rollback compare, T3, recurrence of r2 B5); step-plan contradicts itself on what confirms a criterion (T4) and omits that tests are authored at test-author (T6, two no-op implement visits); implement names exit criteria it does not print (T5); system-test-author promises a host_dependent guard that cannot work for check rows (T7); baseline accepts blank/partial exit records the script could own (T8); the Improve review-focus text never reaches the child contract (T9); Improve parents contradict themselves on reading the skill card (T10); S-15 narrative shown 0 of 4 (T12).

EFFICIENCY. Wall 909.8 s: model generation about 767 s (84%), tool time 142.6 s (15.7%) of which ShipLoop script calls about 100 s (11%). Cost $6.6509 reproduces from tokens (cache read 22.99M = $4.60, cache write $1.04, output $1.01); per-call $0.0554 (r2 $0.0560, r1 $0.0492); the fixed 61.5k-token prefix is $1.48 (22%). No large file was re-read; three one-off whole reads (intake packet, spec-improve packet, improve/SKILL.md, 83k chars) are carried through about 110 later calls (inferred about $0.46).

synthesis.satisfied: Not yet, but close. On this evidence a small, generic, text-level batch is still worth one release; nothing needs a redesign, and everything else is a known limit. Reasoning: the final-batch changes mostly held (A3, A5 computation, A6 reap, the SIGTERM handler, the A2 sentence and all batch-3 items verified working; A1, the A5 refusal and the preflight simply did not fire). Two did not meet their acceptance criteria, each for a concrete reason I confirmed in the files. A2 failed in Battleship because ShipLoop's own integrate row tells the model to commit and then prints a false 'Not committed' notice (R3-1). A4 split: Checkers probed Chrome and retained a real-browser check; Battleship classified the browser case away and ended with a page checked only by markup (R3-6). Of the new findings I would implement five, all small and not tied to any product: R3-1 (integrate wording), R3-2 (the rollback becomes a Done-when line; 3 of 4 runs wrote a non-recipe rollback), R3-3 (one sentence on process and port lifecycle; three rounds in a row, and it killed a sibling run), R3-4 (release-check evidence gate; Battleship's accepted result claimed a confirm run that did not happen), R3-5 (a text fix for the host_dependent guard). I would hold R3-6 and R3-7 for another run (the Grok result and a brownfield case), and document-only everything else, including the Improve-contract review focus, the stale status lines and the harness argv hazard. No run was forced to a pass: Battleship disclosed the browser gap, and Checkers disclosed its own pkill. Stop rule: after those five land in one release, run one Sonnet pair sequenced and not alongside another track, and read the Grok result. Declare the loop done if none of those runs shows a defect that breaks or misleads a normal run, which excludes oracle strength, the Improve ceremony and the other known limits above. Drop the two unsatisfiable criteria: 'no mkdir in a model wrapper' and 'every consumer command carries a floor'."
